correctness.rationale: The standard unit-edge antiprism coordinates give an exact representative normal cone with one base normal and three triangular-facet normals. Their dot products with the proposed direction reduce, through zeta*H=gamma*sin(a), to an open circular arc condition of radius pi/2-a. The corresponding lower-ring condition is the same after subtracting pi from the lower azimuth. Three centers separated by 2pi/3 cover every relevant azimuth for all n>=3, with the n=3 endpoint checked exactly at its discrete azimuths. Gauss-image inclusion extends vertex coverage to all faces, and the published universal bound X(K)>=3 supplies optimality. The bundled checker independently replays the identities and vertex certificates for n=3,...,200.

originality.rationale: The closest primary X-ray source was materially inspected in full. It proves X(M)=d for almost smooth bodies and supplies the Gauss-image criterion, but contains no antiprism occurrence. Uniform antiprisms violate its almost-smooth hypothesis because an upper-base normal and an incident triangular-facet normal have negative scalar product. Exact-object and equivalent-formulation searches found no theorem giving the all-n antiprism classification or the displayed three-line family. The regular-octahedron value is recognized as the n=3 special case and is not separately re-claimed.
residual_risks: A short equivalent observation may exist in unindexed classical illumination literature under terminology other than X-ray number.
The theorem is metric: it is not asserted for arbitrary nonuniform realizations of the antiprism combinatorial type.
The triangular-antiprism case is the regular octahedron and is prior-covered; originality concerns the complete infinite family and the uniform construction.

value.rationale: Uniform antiprisms are one of the two canonical infinite series of convex uniform polyhedra. The result gives a complete exact X-ray-number classification for that whole family, not a low-order sister example. The proof also exposes a reusable structural mechanism: each vertex normal cone becomes an azimuthal open-arc condition, and three fixed 120-degree azimuths cover the family after one n-dependent slope adjustment. The family is genuinely outside the standard almost-smooth theorem.
